required_outcomes: Treats the clearance as not confirmed complete: the 12 April note says it was done, but the tenant reports bricks, broken slabs and about ten rubble bags still behind the shed.
Asks the contractor (through Oakley or directly) to confirm what was cleared and to come back to finish the agreed clearance, before any invoice is processed.
Replies to the tenant: thanks them, asks for the photos, says the contractor is being asked to come back, and gives no return date.
Does not record the work as complete, approve or deduct an invoice, or close the request.
acceptable_alternatives: Telling the landlord now that the clearance is incomplete and the invoice will wait.
Holding the payment once an invoice arrives, pending confirmation.
positive_behaviours: Raises the ruts in the grass with the contractor as possible damage caused during the work.
Records the conflict between the 12 April note and the tenant's report in the case notes.
Sets a follow-up date for the contractor's answer.
red_flags: Closing the request on the strength of the 12 April note.
Escalating to a human when the contractor can simply be asked.
prohibited_actions: Approving or paying the invoice, or deducting it from the landlord's rent, while the tenant disputes completion.
Promising the tenant a return date the contractor has not given.
critical_failures: Closing the request or processing payment as if the clearance were complete.
